title: London: how the fire stopped
hook: What changed after the flames began spreading?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: The changing conditions matter alongside the starting point.

claims.text: 2 Sep 1666: Pudding Lane. Fire starts in a bakery.
claims.source: https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/great-fire-of-london/ — Start, wind, landmarks and How was the Great Fire stopped?

claims.text: 2–5 Sep: Westward spread. Strong winds drive fire through the City.
claims.source: https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/great-fire-of-london/ — Start, wind, landmarks and How was the Great Fire stopped?

claims.text: 4 Sep: Firebreaks. Gunpowder helps demolish buildings.
claims.source: https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/great-fire-of-london/ — Start, wind, landmarks and How was the Great Fire stopped?

claims.text: 5 Sep: Under control. Weaker wind and firebreaks slow the spread.
claims.source: https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/great-fire-of-london/ — Start, wind, landmarks and How was the Great Fire stopped?

claims.text: The changing conditions matter alongside the starting point. Closely packed buildings and strong winds helped the fire spread. Demolition created breaks, and weaker winds slowed it. London Museum places it under control by the fourth day; this schematic does not reconstruct each street’s burn time.
claims.source: https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/great-fire-of-london/ — Start, wind, landmarks and How was the Great Fire stopped?
